subject: Acme Bank — Region pinning & data residency follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmebank.com>, Emily Torres <emily.torres@acmebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-12T15:22:00Z
Subject: Acme Bank — Region pinning & data residency follow-up

Hi Samir / Emily,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning — appreciated the clear rundown of Acme's residency and DR constraints. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can align engineering: 

Call recap / confirmed requirements:
- Production customer data must be pinned to customer region (US for US customers, EU for EU customers).
- Cross-region failover is acceptable only as an exceptional recovery path; all failovers must be logged, audited, and customers notified.
- Backups by default are retained in the same region; Acme is interested in an option for encrypted cross-region snapshots under customer-managed keys for DR.
- Audit logs and request/response logging: Acme needs control over whether logs may contain PII and a clear retention policy (logs retention target ~1 year; some regulated accounts require longer).

Questions / items we promised to follow up on:
1) Confirmation of per-tenant region pinning semantics for hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments.
2) Details on backup replication options and BYOK/KMS support.
3) Clarify what we log by default (request metadata vs full payloads) and how to scrub or avoid PII in logs.
4) Failover process: automatic vs manual, notification hooks, and audit trail granularity.
5) Retention and immutability options for snapshots and logs (regulatory accounts may require 7-year retention for some artifacts).

Attached: region-pinning-overview.pdf (high-level options) and redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (controls overview). I've also put together a short QA table and a proposed deep-dive with our infra/security engineer.

Proposed next steps: 
- I can schedule a technical deep-dive with Marissa (solutions/infra) and our security engineering lead — proposed window: Thursday 2028-09-14 10:00–11:00 ET. If that works for you I'll send an invite.
- If you can confirm RTO/RPO expectations and the set of regulated tenants (if any), we'll prepare concrete config examples and a short table mapping each requirement to recommended deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: region-pinning-overview.pdf, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmebank.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Torres <emily.torres@acmebank.com>, security@acmebank.com
Date: 2028-09-12T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Acme Bank — Region pinning & data residency follow-up

Aditya — thanks for the recap and the materials. A few clarifications from our side so the technical deep-dive is productive: 

Answers / Clarifications from Acme:
- Region pinning: mandatory per-tenant for production (no exceptions), i.e., a tenant whose customers are in the EU must have all production data and backups stored in an EU region.
- Cross-region failover: allowed only for disaster recovery; must be encrypted in transit and at rest, and any failover event must be fully auditable with timestamps + operator ID. We require automated notifications to our security team and an approval flow for any manual failover.
- Backups: daily snapshots stored in-region. For critical/regulatory tenants we require weekly cross-region snapshots encrypted with a separate KMS key (this key should be customer-controlled if possible).
- KMS/BYOK: Acme prefers BYOK for backups and for stored tape/archives. Can Redwood support customer-managed keys in hosted mode, or is that limited to Dedicated/Private?
- Logs: we need to understand what request/response data is logged by default. If request bodies are present in logs, we need a clear mechanism to disable or redact them. Target retention for logs is 12 months, but for some regulated tenants we may need longer retention (up to 7 years) for audit artifacts.

Can you provide a short table answering these explicitly (region pinning per deployment type, BYOK support, backup replication options, default logging behavior, retention/immutability features)? If possible, include whether retention/immutability is possible in hosted or requires Private.

We can do the technical deep-dive Thursday; 10:00 ET works for Emily and me. Please include Marissa from your side and your security engineer.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Cloud Security | Acme Bank
samir.patel@acmebank.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmebank.com>, Emily Torres <emily.torres@acmebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-13T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Acme Bank — Region pinning & data residency follow-up

Samir / Emily — great, thanks for the clarifications and for confirming the Thursday slot. Short answers below (I'll bring Marissa and our security engineer to the deep-dive with more implementation detail):

Short answers table (summary):
- Region pinning: Supported across deployment modes. Hosted API: per-tenant region pinning within our available regions (US/EU/APAC) for Enterprise plans; Dedicated/Private: full per-tenant pinning and network isolation.
- BYOK/KMS: Customer-managed keys supported for Dedicated and Private today; hosted Enterprise supports customer-managed keys via a managed KMS integration (we can bring keys into our HSM boundary or integrate to your cloud KMS for further controls).
- Backup replication: Default = in-region daily snapshots. Cross-region replication available for Dedicated/Private; hosted Enterprise offers cross-region encrypted snapshot replication as an add-on with BYOK support.
- Logging behavior: By default we capture request metadata and non-sensitive headers. Request/response bodies are NOT stored in plaintext logs by default for Enterprise customers; we provide an opt-in config to capture payloads (used rarely and controlled). Redaction hooks and scrubbers are available; Marissa will show config in the deep-dive.
- Retention & immutability: Retention windows configurable per-tenant. Immutable retention (retention locks) available in Private and Dedicated; hosted Enterprise supports configurable retention with legal-hold workflows — for 7-year immutable retention we typically recommend Private or Dedicated with retention lock configuration.

Notes / follow-ups:
- Failover: automatic failover is configurable but we recommend manual approval for tenant-scoped cross-region failover for regulated customers. All failover events generate full audit logs with operator/service account IDs and timestamps; notifications can be sent to your webhook or incident channel.
- KMS keys and separation: we can support customer-controlled KMS for backups and archived snapshots (we'll confirm exact key import or external-KMS flow in the deep-dive).
- Attachments: region-pinning-qa-table.xlsx (short answers table) attached; region-pinning-overview.pdf and redwood-soc2-summary.pdf included again for the meeting.

Next steps (agreed):
1) Deep-dive Thursday 2028-09-14 10:00–11:00 ET — invite will be sent to the attendees.
2) Samir: share list of regulated tenants and target RTO/RPO per tenant (we'll use this to size backup replication and SLA tiers).
3) Marissa + Security Eng: prepare a hosted vs dedicated vs private configuration matrix and illustrate KMS/BYOK flows.
4) I'll follow up with a short written table (HubSpot deal link: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/ACME-2028-044) and the meeting invite.

If anything changes on timing, let me know — otherwise I'll send the invite and include the tech docs.

Best,
Aditya Rao
